newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Products Outlook - Uptrend seen in fuel oil.
newsitem.headline: Asia Products Outlook - Uptrend seen in fuel oil.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market, after being lacklustre for weeks, is expected to see firmer prices this week, while the recent volatile diesel market could take a back seat, traders said on Monday.
The 180-cst grade was offered at $102.50 per tonne at the end of last week, up from $102.00 traded on Thursday and $98.50 a week earlier.
"I won't be surprised if it rises to $104.00 this week," said one trader.

Traders said tighter feul oil supplies from the Middle East, with exporters needing more demand at home for summer air-conditioning and reduced supplies from South Korea because of refinery maintenance schedules May and June, is expected to support the market.
The fuel oil market has been bullish since late last week amid anticipation of fresh demand from a local trader.
Traders said the rise was partly based on the perception by some that the market would be bid higher in coming days to coincide with the arrival of a large cargo from the Gulf.
"The market is fundamentally supported and perception that a local trader may bid up the market further boosts sentiment," said one trader.

The LSWR market is widely expected to maintain its recent bearish tone in the face of slack demand. Indonesia's Pertamina has scheduled 3.85 million barrels of LSWR export allocations for and traders expected an additional 500,000 barrels to be rolled over from April, bringing the May total to 4.35 million barrels.
"I think prices will only pick up in June when summer demand from Japan emerges," said one trader.
In the diesel market, traders said the market is range bound because of some traders' willingness to buy all cargoes offered below $25.50 per barrel but not bidding above this price.
Three traders who are buying have bought more than 19 million barrels of gas oil since the start of March 3.
In the past two weeks the traders, Hin Leong Trading, its sister company Sanko Oil and Japanese trader Marubeni International Petroleum Corp, have lowered their purchase prices to $25.50 from $26.50.
Traders said diesel prices in Asia are poised to test this year's support of $25.00 per barrel, largely due to a steady decline in bid levels by the group of three buyers amid plentiful supplies.
Jet fuel extended its latest slip as refiners continue to offer the market down in the absence of fresh regional enduser demand.
In the light end of the market, naphtha players were mostly distracted by Saudi Aramco term naphtha negotiations scheduled to start Monday.
Discussions would last until Thursday with 13 companies taking turns to meet with Saudi officials.
Saudi Aramco is expected to offer 2.9 million tonnes of light naphtha from Ras Tanura and 1.3 million tonnes of full range naphtha - 800,00 tonnes from Jubail and 500,000 tonnes from Rabigh.
The term cargoes are for lifting between July and December.
Saudi Aramco has set a target premium of $17.00 per tonne while Japanese buyers are mostly holding out at $14-$15 per tonne premium.
Demand from Japan is poor and traders said they did not expect sentiment to improve until late May or early June.
